title: Sanitize route decoder pipeline and add graceful-degradation surge handler
creator: Ayesha Khan
description:
Objective: Reduce cognitive complexity and tail latency in the smart routing layer by sanitizing the route-decoder pipeline and introducing a lightweight surge handler that provides graceful degradation under sudden capacity pressure.

Background: Over the last 18 months the route-decoder (policy input -> routing decision) has accreted ad-hoc predicates, side-channel checks for regional lease state, and implicit weight adjustments that make reasoning about fallback behavior difficult. This increases risk for incorrect fallbacks, complicates telemetry, and contributes to occasional p99 spikes observed during cartesian bursts.

Scope: 
- Implement a dedicated 'decoder sanitizer' stage that normalizes inputs (explicitly validates and canonicalizes route weights, removes deprecated predicates, and maps legacy affinity flags to the new affinity model).
- Move transient checks (lease staleness, temporary circuit markers) out of the pure decoder into a separate ephemeral context that can be short-circuited by the surge handler.
- Add a surge handler that triggers when regional capacity indicators exceed threshold: it will (a) apply conservative weight downscaling for non-critical routes, (b) enable compact fallback path (fast path) with bounded retries, and (c) emit structured telemetry for post-incident analysis.
- Add unit/e2e tests around normalization rules and surge window behavior; add budgeted performance tests for decoder latency.

Non-goals: Rewriting the policy language or adding new customer-facing routing policies. Full migration of all legacy shims is out of scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately.

Success metrics: 
- Decoder median latency reduction >= 10% on typical request mix.
- p99 latency improvement 15% in synthetic burst tests.
- No more than 2% cost regression in throughput-oriented benchmarks.
- Surge handler activates and completes graceful-degradation window in <= 250ms on simulated regional pressure.

Migration and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime-2.7 flag. Canary rollout to 10% of traffic in us-west then widen to 50% pending metrics. Full enable once smoke and perf targets met.
acceptance_criteria: Decoder sanitizer component implemented and exposed as a single composable stage in the smart router pipeline
All legacy predicates in decoder either removed or mapped with explicit comments and transformation tests
Surge handler exists as a configurable policy: threshold, window, downscale factor, and fast-path toggle
Automated unit tests cover weight normalization edge cases and lease-stale branches
Perf job added to CI that records median/p99 for decoder stage and fails on regressions >5%
Canary rollout configuration and rollback playbook documented in Confluence
tasks: Create decoder sanitizer module (sanitizer.go / sanitizer.ts) and API for rule registration
Audit existing predicates and produce canonical mapping table (confluence doc)
Implement surge handler and integrate with regional capacity signals and policy runtime
Add e2e test harness for burst simulation (k6/locust script) and baseline runs
Instrument telemetry: add structured spans/tags for sanitizer, surge decisions, and fast-path counts

Code review and address perf comments, then merge behind runtime-2.7 feature flag
